stem: In a batch of 100 items, 20 are defective. A quality inspector picks one item at random and finds it defective. What is the probability that a second item picked from the remaining 99 is also defective?

per_option_rationale.rationale: After one defective is removed, 19 defectives remain in 99 items. P = 19/99.
Using 20 defectives out of 99 remaining ignores that the first draw removed one defective, giving 20/99.
Using the original proportion 20/100 = 1/5 treats the draws as independent and ignores the conditioning.
Using 19 defectives out of the original 100 forgets to reduce the denominator after the first draw.

explanation:
1. After the first draw, one defective item is removed. The batch has 99 items left, of which 19 are defective.
2. The required probability is conditional on the first item being defective.
3. KEY STEP: P(second defective | first defective) = 19/99.
4. The denominator drops to 99, not 100, because one item has been removed.

explanation_sections.punchline: Sampling without replacement forces two simultaneous updates after each draw: defective count drops from 20 to 19 and pool size drops from 100 to 99. The answer is 19/99.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: conditional probability under sampling without replacement. Assumption: the first draw is confirmed defective, so it is permanently removed. State of the urn after draw 1: 99 items remain, 19 are defective. Required probability = 19/99. Check every distractor against the two-update rule: 20/99 forgets to reduce the defective count; 19/100 forgets to reduce the pool; 1/5 = 20/100 treats draws as independent, ignoring the conditioning entirely.
explanation_sections.lesson: Without replacement means both the numerator (target count) and the denominator (pool size) decrease. Miss either update and you land on a distractor. The four options systematically cover all combinations of updating correctly vs incorrectly.
explanation_sections.timing: 90 seconds. The only arithmetic is a double subtraction: 20 - 1 = 19 and 100 - 1 = 99. Five seconds. Spend the rest confirming the conditioning is applied. Eliminate option 4 first: 1/5 is the pre-draw probability, not the posterior.
